messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B2 | L4 | S4 | C1 | T3 -> 38.6%
B1 | L9 | S3 | C3 | T1 -> 16.9%
B2 | L9 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 16.1%
B2 | L9 | S2 | C1 | T1 -> 7.2%
B3 | L7 | S3 | C2 | T1 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 25 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: Tests whether a modestly higher concentration improves on the best observed conditions while retaining the promising catalyst system and high temperature.
Measures the effect of a further concentration increase under the best observed base, ligand, solvent, and temperature.
Tests whether slightly lower temperature preserves activity while reducing the thermal severity of the best condition.
Checks whether the lead catalyst system can give useful conversion at the lowest temperature.
Assesses the interaction of increased concentration with an intermediate temperature in the lead catalyst system.
Tests a concentrated condition at intermediate temperature to distinguish concentration and temperature effects.
Explores whether higher concentration can compensate for the lowest temperature with the lead catalyst system.
Tests the most concentrated option at low temperature to probe whether concentration can support conversion.
Compares cesium with potassium pivalate directly under the highest-yielding ligand, solvent, concentration, and temperature.
Tests whether cesium acetate improves the lead condition by changing both the alkali-metal cation and carboxylate.
Tests potassium acetate against the lead potassium pivalate condition to isolate the carboxylate effect.
Screens a bulky dialkylaryl phosphine while retaining the other lead-condition variables.
Tests BrettPhos as an alternative bulky, electron-rich biaryl phosphine in the promising reaction environment.
Tests X-Phos to determine whether a different bulky biaryl phosphine improves the lead system.
Evaluates a sterically demanding electron-rich phosphine under the best observed base, solvent, and temperature.
Tests PCy3 HBF4 as an alternative phosphine salt while holding the lead reaction conditions constant.
Compares polar DMAc with the lead ester solvent while preserving the most promising catalyst and operating conditions.
Tests aromatic p-xylene against the lead ester solvent to assess the effect of a less polar medium.
Tests butyronitrile under the lead catalyst conditions to assess a coordinating nitrile solvent.
Checks whether DMAc benefits from a modestly higher concentration at the lead temperature.
Tests the p-xylene solvent at increased concentration to probe solvent–concentration interaction.
Tests whether increased concentration offsets any limitations of the nitrile solvent at high temperature.
Checks whether the cesium-pivalate comparison remains favorable at a modestly higher concentration.
Tests the cesium-acetate condition at higher concentration to evaluate its interaction with reaction concentration.
Tests BrettPhos at increased concentration to see whether its performance depends on the concentration used.
